newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh garment exporters call for cheaper taka.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh garment exporters call for cheaper taka.

text.p: Bangladesh's readymade garment exporters want a substantial devaluation in the local currency the taka to stay competitive in the international markets.

"Bangladesh has failed to match with the neighbouring countries in the devaluation of local currency. Now we exporters are facing the consequence," Mostafa Golam Quddus, president of the Bangladesh Garments Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), told reporters on Saturday night.

Quddus said the value of the taka should be immediately cut by at least 15 percent against the U.S. dollar to prop up the garment sector, which accounts for over 60 percent of the country's export receipts.
"We can expect a rise of our export earning by up to 25 percent if the exchange rate readjusted to 50 taka per dollar instead of the existing 43.30 taka," he said.

The BGMEA chief said Bangladesh had devalued its currency against the U.S. dollar by 23 percent between 1990 and 1996, compared with 104 percent by India, 83 percent by Pakistan and 41 percent by Sri Lanka.
"We are gradually losing competitiveness to the neighbours," Quddus said.
India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka are Bangladesh's major competitors in the international readymade garment market.
The readymade garment sector earned $2.54 billion or 66 percent of Bangladesh's total export receipts in the 1995/96 fiscal year (July-June).
